newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland should consolidate economic stability - OECD.
newsitem.headline: Poland should consolidate economic stability - OECD.

text.p: WARSAW, Oct 18 (Reuer) - Poland needs to strengthen its macroeconomic stability to be able to maintain vigorous growth, the head of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), said on Friday.
OECD Secretary General Donald Johnston told an international investment conference in Warsaw that Poland's main challenge was to slash inflation to one-digit levels within the next two years.
Year-on-year inflation was at 19.5 percent in September against 21.6 percent in December 1995 and the government wants to bring it down to 13 percent next year.
"Consolidating the macroeconomic stabilisation should remain a priority, (as well as)... bringing down inflation to single digits within two years," Johnston said.
"This will require further fiscal consolidation, curbing monetary policy and reforming the social security," he said.
Johnston praised the economic performance of Poland, which was invited to become the OECD's 28th member earlier this year, but said that a great deal still remained to be done.
He noted the goverment should especially pursue privatisation in the banking sector, which needed strengthening. -- Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700
